conventions: Each case gives an input (a Segment as in design section 7.2, plus optional request-level hints and strict_text) and what the design fixes about the outcome.
Only the fields present under expect are asserted. A cue's warnings list, when present, is the complete list of text-check findings for that cue (empty = none).
outcome is ok (the text pipeline accepts the segment) or refused (a tool error; error.code given).
Offsets are Unicode code points. A warning's offset and a hint's offset are into the cue's canonical text (after NFC and whitespace), and an exact span's start/end are into the cue as sent.
unsure lists the paths of expect fields this fixture's author could not fix from the design; note says why. WP10 decides them and updates the fixture.
Invisible or combining characters are written as \u escapes so a reader can see them.

cases.name: canonical_form_collapses_whitespace_runs
cases.about: Every run of whitespace, including no-break and thin spaces, becomes one space; the ends are trimmed.

cases.name: canonical_form_applies_nfc
cases.about: The cue is put in NFC: e + combining acute becomes one code point, and spoken length counts NFC code points.

cases.name: canonical_form_tab_and_newline
cases.about: Tab and newline are whitespace (7.2) and also control characters (9.1 refuses control characters).
cases.note: The design does not say whether tab, newline and carriage return are collapsed as whitespace (7.2) or refused as control characters (9.1 step 1 runs before canonical form). This fixture assumes they are whitespace and only other control characters are refused; WP10 decides.

cases.name: canonical_form_adds_no_punctuation_or_capital
cases.about: Nothing but whitespace and Unicode form changes: no capital and no full stop are added.

cases.name: join_is_cues_joined_by_one_space
cases.about: The join is the cues' canonical texts joined by one space; nothing is added at a cue boundary.

expect.spoken: The ferry left at dawn, and nobody saw it go.
expect.engine: The ferry left at dawn, and nobody saw it go.

cases.note: Each cue's span in the join is written here as [start, end) in code points; the field's name and shape are WP10's.

cases.name: join_uses_canonical_cues
cases.about: Each cue is canonicalised before the join.

cases.name: text_only_segment_is_one_cue
cases.about: A segment sent as text only is one cue, in canonical form.

cases.name: text_equal_to_join_is_accepted
cases.about: A text equal to the join of the cues is accepted.

cases.name: text_whose_canonical_form_equals_join_is_accepted
cases.about: The comparison is on canonical forms, so extra spaces and a no-break space in text do not matter.

cases.name: text_differing_only_in_nfc_is_accepted
cases.about: A decomposed character in text and a composed one in the cue have the same canonical form.

cases.name: text_differing_from_join_is_refused
cases.about: A text whose canonical form differs from the join (here: no full stop) is refused.
cases.note: The field path format is WP01/WP17's; the design fixes only the code.

cases.name: spoken_length_counts_code_points_not_utf16_units
cases.about: Four Gothic letters are four code points (eight UTF-16 units); spoken length counts code points.

cases.name: spoken_length_ignores_hints
cases.about: Hints change the engine text, not the spoken text, so spoken length is unchanged.

cases.name: hint_matches_whole_words_only
cases.about: A term matches only where it stands as a whole word: not inside Tarnholm, but before a full stop.

cases.name: hint_matches_case_sensitively
cases.about: Terms match case-sensitively: Tarn does not match tarn.

cases.name: hint_longest_term_first
cases.about: Velmora Pass is matched before Velmora, and Velmora still matches where it stands alone.

cues.text: Velmora Pass is closed, but Velmora itself is open.

cues.spoken: Velmora Pass is closed, but Velmora itself is open.
cues.engine: Vell-mora Pass is closed, but Vell-mora itself is open.

cases.note: Offsets are assumed to be code points into the cue's spoken (canonical) text; in the engine text the second application is at a different offset. The order of hints_applied (by offset here) is also WP10's.

cases.name: hint_possessive_replaces_the_term_only
cases.about: The apostrophe bounds a word, so Oskarin matches in Oskarin's and only the term is replaced.

cases.name: hint_possessive_with_curly_apostrophe
cases.about: The same with a right single quotation mark as the apostrophe.

cases.name: hint_bounded_by_hyphen
cases.about: A hyphen is punctuation, so Tarn matches in Tarn-side.
cases.note: Assumes the hyphen counts as punctuation for the whole-word rule, as the passing punctuation list suggests.

cases.name: hint_multiword_term_matches_after_canonical_form
cases.about: Hints are matched in the canonical cue, where the run of spaces is one space.

cues.text: We crossed Velmora   Pass at noon.

cues.spoken: We crossed Velmora Pass at noon.
cues.engine: We crossed Vell-mora Pass at noon.

cases.name: hint_never_applied_across_a_cue_boundary
cases.about: A term that would match only across a cue boundary is not applied and is flagged.

expect.engine: We climbed towards Velmora Pass before noon.

cases.name: hint_offsets_are_per_cue
cases.about: A term is matched inside each cue, and each application records its offset in that cue.

expect.engine: Oss-kah-rin rowed out. Oss-kah-rin came back.

cases.name: hint_without_respelling_leaves_engine_text
cases.about: A term sent without a respelling leaves the engine text as the spoken text.

cases.name: warn_digit
cases.about: An ASCII digit is a digit warning; the text is not changed.

cases.name: warn_digit_other_script
cases.about: A digit from another script (ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT THREE) is a digit warning.

cases.name: warn_digit_superscript
cases.about: A superscript digit is a digit warning.

cues.text: Mark it with a small ² in the margin.

cases.note: A digit is also 'not a letter', so a literal reading of the symbol rule would flag it twice. These fixtures expect one warning per token, of kind digit.

cases.name: warn_symbols
cases.about: Each symbol the design names is a symbol warning: & % / × ° · # and a currency sign.

cues.text: Salt & pepper , ten % more , up / down , four × four , ten ° warmer , dot · dot , room # nine , one £ coin .

cases.name: warn_symbol_inside_a_word
cases.about: A symbol inside a token is still a symbol warning.
cases.note: Whether token is the whole token (north/south) or the character (/), and which offset is reported, is WP10's.

cases.name: pipe_and_angle_bracket_alone_warn_not_refused
cases.about: Only the pairs <| and |> are refused as markup; a lone | or < is a symbol warning.

cases.name: warn_unit_like
cases.about: Tokens in the generic unit list, matched case-sensitively, are unit_like warnings.

cues.text: A walk of ten km , four kg , sixty mph , nine ft , fifty Hz , two kW today.

cases.name: warn_unit_like_before_punctuation
cases.about: A unit token followed by a full stop is still unit_like.

cases.name: warn_unit_like_lone_lower_case_m_s_g
cases.about: The lone lower-case unit letters m, s and g are unit_like, not letter.

cues.text: A rise of two m , wait five s , add ten g now.

cases.name: no_warning_for_a_A_I_in_am
cases.about: a, A and I are not lone-letter findings, and in and am are ordinary words, not units.

cues.text: A cat and I am in a boat.

cases.name: lone_capitals_are_letter_info
cases.about: A lone capital other than A and I is a letter finding at severity info.

cues.text: Plan B failed, so we tried C and then J.

cases.note: C is also the symbol for the coulomb; unit_like needs two or more characters, except m, s and g.

cases.name: lone_lower_case_letters_are_letter_info
cases.about: A lone lower-case letter other than a, m, s and g is a letter finding at severity info.

cues.text: Mark the spot with an x and an e.

cases.name: passing_punctuation_raises_no_warning
cases.about: Every mark a reader voices as prosody passes: . , ; : ! ? ' ’ ‘ " “ ” ( ) - – — …

cues.text: He said, "Wait — the tide… it's turning; isn’t it?" ‘Yes’: the east–west road (quiet) is a well-worn path! “Go.”

cues.spoken: He said, "Wait — the tide… it's turning; isn’t it?" ‘Yes’: the east–west road (quiet) is a well-worn path! “Go.”
cues.engine: He said, "Wait — the tide… it's turning; isn’t it?" ‘Yes’: the east–west road (quiet) is a well-worn path! “Go.”

cases.name: strict_text_refuses_warnings
cases.about: With strict_text, a text warning refuses the request instead, listing every offender.
cases.note: How the offenders are listed (error.details) is WP01/WP10's; the design says every offender is listed.

cases.name: strict_text_and_letter_info
cases.about: A lone letter is info, not a warning, so strict_text is assumed not to refuse it.
cases.note: The design says strict_text refuses on text warnings; whether an info-level letter finding counts is WP10's.

cases.name: exact_span_offsets_are_code_points_in_accented_text
cases.about: Offsets count code points: ë and ï are one code point each.

cues.text: Zoë and Anaïs counted forty-two cranes.

cases.note: word_range is [first, end) in whitespace-separated words of the cue; the stored form is WP10's.

cases.name: exact_span_offsets_are_code_points_beyond_the_bmp
cases.about: Letters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane are one code point each (two UTF-16 units).

cases.name: exact_span_word_range_survives_canonical_form
cases.about: Offsets are into the cue as sent (before canonical form); the span is kept as a word range.

cases.name: exact_span_over_several_words
cases.about: A span may cover several whole words.

cues.text: They counted three hundred and twelve geese.

cases.name: exact_span_may_end_before_trailing_punctuation
cases.about: A span may end before trailing punctuation.

cases.name: exact_span_may_end_after_trailing_punctuation
cases.about: A span may end after trailing punctuation; punctuation is ignored in the comparison.
cases.note: Whether words echoes seven or seven. is WP10's; the span is valid either way.

cases.name: exact_span_may_start_before_leading_punctuation
cases.about: A span starting on the opening bracket of (forty) is on a word edge, as punctuation is set aside.
cases.note: The design says a span may end before or after trailing punctuation; this assumes the same for leading punctuation.

cases.name: exact_span_that_cuts_a_hyphenated_word_is_refused
cases.about: forty-two is one word, so a span over forty alone cuts it and is refused.

cases.name: exact_span_that_cuts_letters_is_refused
cases.about: A span that starts inside a word is refused.

cases.name: exact_spans_that_overlap_are_refused
cases.about: Spans must not overlap.

cues.text: They counted three hundred and twelve geese.

cases.name: exact_span_outside_the_cue_is_refused
cases.about: A span must lie inside the cue.

cases.name: exact_span_that_is_empty_is_refused
cases.about: A span with start equal to end covers no word.
cases.note: The schema allows start 0 and end 1 at minimum; start < end is assumed.

cases.name: markup_square_brackets_are_refused
cases.about: [ and ] are refused, as the engine could take them as markup; every offender is listed.

cases.name: markup_special_token_delimiters_are_refused
cases.about: <| and |> are refused.

cases.name: control_character_nul_is_refused
cases.about: A control character (NUL) is refused.

cases.name: control_character_bell_is_refused
cases.about: A control character (BEL) is refused.

cases.name: control_character_escape_is_refused
cases.about: A control character (ESC) is refused.

cases.name: control_character_delete_is_refused
cases.about: A control character (DEL) is refused.

cases.name: control_character_c1_csi_is_refused
cases.about: A control character (the C1 control CSI) is refused.

cases.name: markup_in_a_later_cue_is_refused
cases.about: Every cue is sanitised, not only the first.
